recipes.name: Sweet Pork Slow Cooker Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 (11 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained

steps.text: Cook the ground pork in a skillet over medium heat until completely browned; drain.

Combine the cooked pork, tomato, bell pepper, pineapple, beans, kernel corn, tomato paste, onion, baby corn, cider, garlic, brown sugar, salt, paprika, pepper, molasses, ancho chile pepper, sage, curry powder, cinnamon, honey, and vinegar in a large slow cooker; stir.
Set slow cooker to High. Cook at least 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Pork Slow Cooker Chili
raw_recipe.description: This chili recipe for the slow cooker makes a slightly-sweet and mild dish that can easily be adjusted for your personal tastes.

review.reviewBody: This was a great chili! I modified it a bit and added chili powder, crushed red pepper & a couple of fresh hot peppers because I like my chili to be spicy and it was a perfect sweet&spicy mix. I brought my modified recipe to a chili cookoff and won "most unique".

I loved this recipe!! It's totally a different kind of chili. You taste the sweet and hot, but nothing specifically screams there's pineapple in here! I even ground mine in the food processor so that it was really hidden because I'm not sure my husband would have eaten chili with pineapple -which he totally loved it by the way. I didn't have 2lbs pork so I used 1lb pork and 1 lb turkey. Turned out great!!

We really enjoyed this delicious and different chili recipe. Loved the sweet/savory/salty going on here, especially the addition of the pineapple, yum! With an ingredient list this big I did make a few tweaks based on what I had, used 1 lb ground pork and 1 lb ground chicken (I use this mix in a sloppy joe recipe i make and love the texture and cuts a few calories), a 15 oz can of fire roasted tomatoes instead of the romas, an 8oz can of tomato sauce instead of paste, and doubled the curry, love the stuff. I also added a couple of heaping tablespoons of sambal oleek for some heat. Lots left over for the freezer. Thanks for sharing your recipe with AR, a hit!

Didn't have hard apple cider. So substituted 2tbsp cider vinegar and a 14oz can of tomato sauce. And added back some of the (crushed) pineapple juice I had drained. Cut back to 8oz tomato paste. Still a thick meaty chili! DO NOT skip the pinch of cinnamon or the curry. This is the mosy flavorful chili I have ever had. You can actually taste each of the ingrediants.

This was very good..I made some changes just because I didn't have the apple cider so I used the juice from the can of pineapple and a small can of pineapple juice. Also instead of using fresh tomatoes I threw in a can of rotel which spiced the chili up...I didn't need to add any more hot sauce. I really like the pineapple in the chili...I would definitely make this again

DH & I just made this today in the crockpot. We were a little concerned about the flavour combination but it turned out amazing! It smelled soooo good while cooking, we could hardly wait to try it. You get - salty, sweet, spicy. We added about 2 lbs of pork chops, cut up and 1 lb of pork sausage meat (no casings). We used a can of crushed pineapple, not drained. Thisis a great recipe that we'll be making again. Give it a try, you won't regret it.

I made this with only a few little changes and it turned out incredible, it is definitely going into my meal rotation! I substituted out regular onions for the green onions since I didn't have any, added one more clove of garlic (mine were small), and added a fair bit of chili powder so it was mildly spicy. Turned out perfect! Very flavorful and excellent with some cheese melted on top.

I made this yesterday for the Saints game with the following changes...I used 1lb. of turkey instead of 2lb of pork and I used the pinapple juice from the can instead of the hard apple cider. It was SOOOOO GOOD!!! I will make this again and again!
Not what you expect when you hear "chili" but it's freakin' awesome! I cut the honey by about a third and added a tablespoon of maple syrup (I'm Canadian and couldn't resist)

Wow- loved this recipe even more than I was expecting! I used regular chili powder and paprika and forgot the brown sugar (oops!) but it was still phenomenal! I added 2 diced jalapenos since I like my chili spicy and it was the perfect balance of sweet and spicy. 

I served it with shredded cheddar and sour cream. I also mixed half the leftovers with brown rice and brought it for lunch during the week. Both veriations lended well to the chili. I will definitely make this again. It is a unique dish that will surprise you. I would definitely reccommend it for a pot luck as it is a definite crowd pleaser!

I admit, I made some changes to this based on what I had available, but I stuck to the recipe as much as I could and think it turned out pretty tasty. It had a nice sweet flavor to it and it was definitely a change of pace. I served with cheddar cheese on top and cornbread on the side. The changes I made were: 1)cubed pork loin chops in place of ground pork, that I browned lightly before adding to the slow cooker 2)canned tomato in place of fresh, one drained can per tomato called for 3)Slightly less pineapple than called for 4)additional corn kernels in place of baby corn 5)apple juice in place of apple cider 6)additional brown sugar in place of molasses 7)I knew I would be cooking this for 7 hours, so I cooked on low instead of high.

It was absolutely horrible, so unbalanced. 
I grew up eating Cuban food, so I am used to sweet and savory together.
This recipe is worth making. I didn’t have green onions so I just used some sweet onions. I also substituted the pepper spice. I will definitely make this again
Smells so good and tastes unusually good!
I don't care for spicy food so this was a nice alternative. I will make it again.
Was a little too sweet for our taste
Outstanding!
We enjoyed this. It was a nice twist on chilli.

I substituted molasses with honey and used regular apple cider. I used pork shoulder chucks instead of ground pork. I followed everything else according to recipe. Cooked in slow cooker all day. The taste was good, a little sweet, a little spicy, a little tomatoey because of the tomato paste. My husband liked it. My daughter thought it was OK but she prefers he ground beef chilli that I normally make. My sons did not like it at all. I thought it was just OK. It was easy but you have to buy all those ingredients and mix all the spices in which can be time consuming. I don't think I'll be making this again but it was good to try something different.
I make this exact, EXACT, recipe often. Love it.
